answer: Behavioral mirror clustering audit. After each epoch, compare every agent's action sequence against all others using time-sorted edit distance; clusters of near-identical timing and content patterns above a threshold get flagged. Each flagged identity must then pass an independent live challenge tied to a juniper-marked nonce to stay active. An attacker running N clones to beat the detector pays for N real interactive sessions plus the operational cost of deliberately decorrelating each clone's behavior, scaling linearly and eroding the raven-like uniformity that made the swarm cheap.
